name: LaMa (big-lama inpainting)
plain: LaMa big-lama (Suvorov et al., Samsung AI, WACV 2022): fills the masked hole of an image (object removal) with a fast-Fourier-convolution network trained on scene photos. Apache-2.0 code and weights; the Places365 training images are for research use only (see the card).
summary: LaMa (Suvorov et al., WACV 2022): resolution-robust large-mask inpainting with fast Fourier convolutions: an encoder of three strided convs, 18 FFC residual blocks whose global branch convolves in the frequency domain (an image-wide receptive field from the first block) and a transposed-conv decoder. big-lama (51 M parameters) is the authors' best model, trained on Places365 at 256 x 256 and works at higher resolutions. Pass `mask=` (nonzero = the region to fill); the rest of the image is kept unchanged.

papers.title: Resolution-robust Large Mask Inpainting with Fourier Convolutions

limitations: No accuracy measurement: inpainting is scored on Places / CelebA-HQ with the authors' random masks, which are not part of the evaluation data here; tiers are compared by output parity and speed only.
Fills the masked region from the surrounding image; it does not take a text prompt. The authors' refinement step (`refine=True`, an iterative multi-scale optimisation) is not implemented.
Any nonzero mask pixel is a hole (upstream binarises with `mask > 0`): anti-aliased or JPEG masks grow; threshold them first.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: the restored (upscaled) image, `model.scale` x the input size, RGB in [0, 1]. `tile=` runs large images in overlapping tiles (as ComfyUI).

variants.name: big-lama

licence.training_note: big-lama: Places365-Challenge (about 4.5 M images used) with LaMa's random wide / box masks, 256 x 256 crops (paper Sec. 4 and README).

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 16, padded to a multiple of 8

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

kernels.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: .half() on 1 modules, fp16 inputs; advimman/lama@786f5936b27f FFCResNetGenerator, predict.py padding / masking / paste-back

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.002 and p99 <= 0.01 (absolute error of the output `image`).
